newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S&P says places Tarkett on CreditWatch.
newsitem.headline: S&P says places Tarkett on CreditWatch.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday it placed German flooring products company Tarkett Aktiengesellschaft on CreditWatch with negative implications following the acquisition of a unit of Sommer Allibert.
Tarkett AG said earlier on Wednesday it was merging its worldwide floor covering business with that of French group Sommer Allibert SA.
Tarkett said it would buy Sommer Allibert's floor covering division -- excluding floor coverings for motor vehicles -- for 705 million marks in cash.

"The acquisition, which will be purely debt-financed, will weaken Tarkett's financial structure and raise net debt to capital to 74 percent (up from 33 percent) on a proforma basis," S&P said in a statement.
Hence, although the acquisition will have a positive impact on Tarkett's business profile, the financial risk will increase beyond what was anticipated in the rating," it said.
S&P said a review was needed before any change to the ratings, which were BBB for corporate credit and BBB- for subordinated debt.

"Prior to any ratings change, Standard & Poor's will review Tarkett's credit quality in light of the updated operating and financial strategies and study the relationships with its new majority owner upon the final completion of this operation."
